Subject: Post-call: model fit & eval next steps (Acme AI)

Thanks for the time today — great conversation. Quick recap and proposed next steps from our discovery on Acme's summarization / assist use case:

- Goal: Improve accuracy and reduce hallucination on product-spec summarization for internal docs. Primary constraints: sub-300ms P95 latency, high factuality with conservative temperature, and on-prem/private deployment in future.
- Observations: Your prompt set (shared during call) tends to push the model to be more creative; some of the top-line metrics we saw in the quick eval were NER F1 0.78 and factuality score ~0.82 on the subset you provided.

Recommended model profiles to try:
- redwood-rt-2.7b-quant (recommended starter for cost/latency)
- open-llama-13b-v2 (if you want higher baseline factuality; note higher infra)

Attached: acme_benchmark_report_20260720.pdf (summary of quick eval) and prompt_set_v1.csv (the prompts you shared + our suggested conservative variants).

Next steps (proposed):
1) We’ll run a focused eval using your canonical prompts (we’ll use the conservative variants in prompt_set_v1.csv) and return detailed diffs + example failure cases. (Target: 2 business days)
2) If we see quality regressions tied to model variants, we can either pin to a previous model version for your production route or perform a rollback. Dev will confirm options/timeline.
3) Follow-up 30-minute sync with your ML lead and our SE (Dev) to review the diffs and alignment on rollouts.

Can you confirm the eval scope (full dataset vs sample) and availability for a quick sync later this week?

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.ai | (415) 555-0192

--

Hi Evan —

Short answer: we can isolate and we have a proposed mitigation.

What we did so far:
- Ran the 500-sample eval on your canonical prompts (thanks for sharing) and produced per-prompt diffs. See eval_diffs_20260722.txt attached and the quick summary below.
- Observation: the regression you saw maps to the new kernel/quantization path we enabled for redwood-rt-2.7b-quant on 2026-07-15. That path improves P95 latency but the quantization interaction (int8 fused kernels) changed tokenization edge cases for numeric/tabular contexts — producing higher hallucination rates on some prompts.

Metrics (sample of regressions):
- Prompt category: numeric-tables -> factuality drop from 0.87 -> 0.72
- Average token-level perplexity increased 12% on the affected prompts

Mitigations we can do quickly:
1) Pin your production route to model@redwood-rt-2.7b-quant@v20260701 (pre-quant-kernel) — immediate fix, minimal infra change.
2) Rollback the platform-wide kernel change for routes that opt-in — needs a short change window and SRE approval (ETA 4-6 hours once approved).
3) Patch the quant kernels & tokenizer edge-case handling — engineering work (ETA ~2 weeks) to validate and upstream fix.

If you want the immediate fix, give us authorization to pin your route to the pre-change model version. We’ll coordinate a short maintenance window (we can do off-peak hours).

Attached: eval_diffs_20260722.txt

—Dev
